text:
Owen: Hi all, new hire in the UK. WireGuard connects fine but I can't ssh from office to my dev box at home for pairing. I tried `ssh <me>@<home-ip>` but connection refused and my home router shows a private WAN IP (100.x.x.x). Anyone seen ISP CGNAT break inbound flows?
IT-ops: welcome! yes that 100.64.0.0/10 is CGNAT range. If your ISP puts you behind CGNAT you don't have a publicly-routable WAN IP, so inbound connects to your home box won't work. WireGuard being split-tunnel complicates this because we don't NAT your home traffic through Redwood by default.
Owen: oh makes sense. I need inbound occasionally (pairing, live demo). What's the easiest way to get remote-access without changing ISP?
devops-bot: Tip: Two common approaches for onboarding folks behind CGNAT: (1) use an outbound reverse tunnel via the bastion (SSH -R) from your home box to bastion so colleagues can connect, (2) use the bastion as a SOCKS/HTTP proxy for dev tools, or (3) request a temporary full-tunnel VPN profile while we assess a permanent fix.
Samira: if you can run a persistent reverse tunnel from your dev box it's pretty simple. On your home machine run: ```ssh -N -R 2222:localhost:22 bastionsvc@bastion.redwood``` then teammates can `ssh -p 2222 bastionsvc@bastion.redwood` to reach your box (we have an auth wrapper that forwards to the reverse tunnel). We auto-rotate keys and monitor tunnels.
Owen: sweet. Any security caveats?
Samira: we only allow reverse tunnels from approved onboarding accounts and we terminate them in a sandboxed proxy that logs access. Open a ticket so IT can whitelist your user for reverse-tunnel usage. Ticket tag: ONB-5340 `cgnat-reverse-tunnel`.
Vik: alternatively, for quick demos you can just run `ssh -J bastionsvc@bastion.redwood bastionsvc@10.4.22.34` to hop to internal hosts. But that doesn't help if someone outside wants to reach your laptop directly.
Owen: tried the `ssh -N -R` command; it connects but I'm not sure how teammates find me. Do they use my username?
IT-ops: they `ssh -p 2222 <your-username>@bastion.redwood`. We map the reverse port to your username once you register the tunnel in the onboarding form (link provided in ticket).
Owen: nice. setup completed and my colleague could connect. Thanks!
devops-bot: Note: we also provide a managed option for long-term needs where we proxy incoming traffic through a customer-facing relay service. Request `cgnat-relay` via ONB-5340 if you need a persistent public endpoint.
Vik: FYI if you need to share web apps quickly, `ssh -R 8080:localhost:3000 bastionsvc@bastion.redwood` lets people open `http://bastion.redwood:8080` to reach your local webserver. Be careful to stop forwarding when done.
Owen: Logging issue for ticket ONB-5340. I'll keep the reverse tunnel running while I finish onboarding tasks. Appreciate the help and the warm welcome :raised_hands:
